sentence: HLA-B*57:01 (carriers/positive) is associated with increased risk of abacavir hypersensitivity when treated with abacavir in people with HIV infection in the Western Australian HIV Cohort Study as compared to HLA-B*57:01–negative individuals.
explanation: In a cohort of abacavir-exposed HIV patients (retrospective n=200; prospective n=48; 18 hypersensitive, 230 tolerant), the study confirmed a strong association of HLA-B*57:01 with definite abacavir hypersensitivity; the combination of HLA-B*57:01 with Hsp70-Hom M493T was present in 94.4% of hypersensitive cases versus 0.4% of controls, supporting HLA-B*57:01 as a key marker of risk.
citations: We now report the results of fine recombinant genetic mapping in an expanded patient population of 248 consecutive, fully ascertained, abacavir-exposed individuals in the Western Australian HIV Cohort Study, in which 18 cases of definite abacavir hypersensitivity (7.3%) and 230 tolerant controls were identified.

With regard to alleles specific to the 57.1 AH, *HLA-B*5701* was present in 17 of 18 (94.4%) cases with abacavir hypersensitivity and 4 of 230 (1.7%) abacavir-tolerant controls [OR = 960, *P* value corrected for the number of alleles examined (*P*_c_) < 0.0001].
*HLA-B*5701* was present in 94.4% of hypersensitive cases compared with 1.7% of controls (odds ratio, 960; P < 0.00001).
Hence, the incidence of abacavir hypersensitivity among *HLA-B*5701*-negative individuals in this prospective cohort was 0% (95% confidence interval, 0–0.075%).

explanation: The allele is referenced as part of the 57.1 ancestral haplotype used for screening, but the paper does not report an independent analysis of HLA-DRB1*07:01 with abacavir hypersensitivity or other abacavir outcomes.
